subject: general
question: Which of the following possesses the largest isolated single cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ostrich egg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **ostrich egg** is the largest isolated single cell in nature, with an average weight of around 1.4 kg and a diameter of approximately 15–18 cm.
 
• It is classified as a single cell because it contains the female ostrich's ovum, making it a reproductive cell (gamete).
 
• The shell of the ostrich egg is strong and thick, measuring about 2–4 mm in thickness, to support its large size and protect it from external damage.
 
• Despite its size, the ostrich egg is relatively small compared to the body size of the ostrich, which is the largest bird in the world.
 
• It takes about 42 days for an ostrich egg to hatch, and it can withstand a weight of up to 120 kg without breaking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Definition:** A cell is the basic unit of life in all living organisms. In the case of an ostrich egg, the entire egg (excluding the shell) is a single cell with a nucleus.
 
• **Gametes:** These are reproductive cells that unite during fertilization to form a new organism. The ostrich egg is the female gamete, while the sperm is the male gamete.
 
• **Largest Animal Cells:** In addition to the ostrich egg, other large cells in the animal kingdom include certain types of neurons in whales and squids.
 
• **Blue Whale and Amoeba:** While the blue whale is the largest animal, its cells are not unusually large. Amoeba, though a single-celled organism, is much smaller than an ostrich egg.
 
• **Structural Support:** The ostrich egg’s shell is made of calcium carbonate, providing protection and structural integrity, essential for embryonic development.
